data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The three consecutive even integers are 44, 46, and 48, making 48 the largest.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If 138 were not divisible by 3, then the middle value would not be an integer and no such triple of consecutive even integers would exist.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 138 divided by 3 yielded an odd number (e.g. 141/3 = 47), the resulting triple (45, 47, 49) would be odd, not even, and the even-constraint would fail.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the problem did not require the integers to be even (allowing any consecutive integers), the answer would be different.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Let the middle even integer be x. The three consecutive even integers are x-2, x, and x+2. The sum is (x-2) + x + (x+2) = 3x. Setting 3x = 138 yields x = 46. The three integers are 44, 46, and 48. This works because the constant difference of 2 between consecutive even integers causes the -2 and +2 to cancel exactly, making the sum equal to three times the middle value.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
